title: Conflicts Between the Group and the Local Entity
summary: Where the interests of the group and a regulated subsidiary diverge, from capital and liquidity transfers to pricing, client allocation and strategy, and how directors identify, manage and record those conflicts.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Where the interests of the group and a regulated subsidiary diverge, from capital and liquidity transfers to pricing, client allocation and strategy, and how directors identify, manage and record those conflicts.
Learning Objectives: Identify common conflicts between group and local entity interests
Apply a structured approach to managing and recording group conflicts
Challenge group decisions that disadvantage the entity, its customers or its regulators
Syllabus: Intragroup funding, dividends, guarantees and transfer pricing
Client allocation, product shelf and revenue sharing across entities
Local directors' conflicts when they also hold group roles
Case study: a group restructuring the local board does not support
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated subsidiaries, and of parent and holding companies
Country heads, branch managers and senior managers responsible for a local entity within a wider group
Group and local heads of compliance, risk, legal, governance and regulatory affairs
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board, senior management or control function experience in a firm that is part of a group or operates across borders is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)
